messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each request. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the user wants multiple facilities per query: reading room and fiction; Wi-Fi and children section; cafe and reading room. The function signature only allows a single facility? It says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That seems ambiguous: maybe it expects an array? But the type says "Cafe"[] meaning array of Cafe? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates array of strings? The type is weird. Possibly they want to pass an array of facilities. But the type says union of string or array? Let's interpret: facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[] means either one of those strings or an array of "Cafe"? That doesn't make sense. Maybe it's a mistake. We'll assume we can pass an array of strings. So we will call the function three times:

1. location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We need to produce calls to the function. Then we need to output the results. The function returns any. We'll just call it.
